solutes.model: ideal equilibrium stages; fresh equal solvent portions; constant dilute-solution distribution coefficient; only free I2 partitions, aqueous-only I3- with I- re-equilibrated after each stage
solutes.provenance: K = 26.0 (molar, [I2]hexane/[I2]water, 25 °C), DERIVED as the ratio of saturation concentrations, which equals the partition coefficient up to the negligible mutual solubility of hexane and water: I2 mole fraction 0.00456 in n-hexane (molar volume 131.6 cm3/mol) -> 0.0347 M, Hildebrand & Scott, The Solubility of Nonelectrolytes, 3rd ed. (1950), p. 274, Table 1 'Iodine Solutions, 25°C' (as read from archive.org solubilityofnone0000joel); aqueous solubility 0.3393 g/L (1.334e-3 M) at 25 °C: Hartley & Campbell, J. Chem. Soc. Trans. 93 (1908) 741-745, doi:10.1039/CT9089300741. The same ratio for CCl4 gives 88.5 against Jakowkin's measured 89.6 (Z. physik. Chem. 18 (1895) 585, as tabulated by Hildebrand & Scott p. 208), which checks the method; the earlier K = 85 cited an exam question and was the CCl4 value. Neither source gives a temperature model; I2 + I- <=> I3-, K = 698 L/mol at 25 °C: Palmer, Ramette & Mesmer, J. Solution Chem. 13 (1984) 673, doi:10.1007/BF00650374; only free I2 partitions, I3- stays in water
